quest.title: The Recollector's Path
quest.description: After bringing Mihir and Rashnu back to the Vourukasha Oasis, Sorush finally earned the approval of the Khvarena, gaining the Twin-Horned Chaplet and becoming the Bloomguard. But with regard to the responsibilities of such a position, Zurvan seems to have a few things to say...\n
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x10, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's getting so used to how you look now that Paimon can't even remember what you looked like without the Chaplet, Sorush.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmmm... Paimon seems to recall some baldness at the top of your head and a haughty disposition...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But Paimon didn't expect you to get the Chaplet so easily... Though it was mostly thanks to our help, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Bah! Mention the trifles of the past no more, Pale Floater. The thing of greatest importance, the reason why we were able to claim the Chaplet so easily...

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Was because I am a Pari worthy of the Twin-Horned Chaplet. Hence, everything fell into place as it was meant to be. Perhaps I was fated to bear this crown from the day of my birth.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: A familiar voice comes from behind...

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Hehe, bragging loudly, I see.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: E—Elder Zurvan! What brings you here?

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Just seeing if our newest Bloomguard is fulfilling her duties.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: D—Duties...

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Oh, no. Did you think claiming such a title would bring you nothing but fame and fortune, Sorush?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Impossible! I am no Pari of rank ignorance. The duties I have... have not been neglected. Indeed, I have also performed the necessary feats to be worthy of my accolades.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Though the flashing flame might steal your attention, a gradual trickle of enduring devotion may also be worthy of praise.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Ugh...

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: In the time you have spent away from us, there have been countless Pari who, though unable to ever gain the title of "Bloomguard," still contribute to our greater community with quiet dignity.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Uhh...

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: I thought that you would perform some deeds that would prove your worthiness of the title of "Bloomguard." As it turns out, however, it seems you're just been idling about.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hey! Saying she does nothing is going too far. Sorush is already pretty great! Right, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: I did not mean to neglect my duties... It's just that the responsibilities of a Bloomguard weren't... fully detailed by the Order of Skeptics...

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: It is a Pari tradition, after all. Trying to learn it from humans is pure folly.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Though you have earned the approval of the Khvarena, you remain a young Pari. In times like these, it is best to be direct and consult me for guidance.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Ask you for guidance directly, Elder? But... No, the Chaplet possesses a great deal of knowledge, I need but contemplate for a moment before I am greeted with answers...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But Zurvan is right here. She even said that if we have questions, she will answer... We don't even need to go hunting for details anymore!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #From Paimon and {NICKNAME}'s deep adventuring experience, chances like this are pretty few. You'll regret not taking this opportunity!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: I doubt not my elder's sincerity, it's just... I heard the Order of Skeptics say that only the answers one finds themselves are worth any merit.

choices.text: Isn't that something someone else told you as well?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah. Do you really think the Order of Skeptics is more trustworthy than Zurvan?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: ...Indeed. You offer truth in your insights, Yasnapati, Pale Floater.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: I am no longer the Sorush from before. With the Khvarena's approval, I must act with maturity and live up to the title of Bloomguard.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Ahem. Zurvan... I mean, Elder Zurvan. What are the exact obligations that a Bloomguard must fulfill? I beg of you to enlighten me. Though I have been neglectful in the past, I will do my utmost now to remedy my failings.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa. Paimon didn't expect Sorush to be so obedient. What happened? Paimon feels a little touched!

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Haha... Well, your words give me confidence. The Bloomguard's duties are vast, and may take days and nights to recall in their totality...

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: However, considering that you have spent far more time with the humans than those of your own kind, let's start with something simple.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: As for all those who bear the title of Bloomguard, extraordinary competence and keen insight are necessities.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: I've already prepared six training tasks, with three meant to test flying skills, and the other three... well, they'll need Sorush to clear out some potential threats.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: This training sounds kind of familiar...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds familiar? It IS familiar. Isn't this just something we do all the time...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Enough talk, Pale Floater. As long as I successfully finish these missions, my elder must concede that I am worthy and prepared for the mantle of Bloomguard.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Though it sounds simple, these are all tests delivered unto me by my elder. I must unleash my fullest effort when dealing with them.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: #Hehe, very good. Very good. Conveniently, Sorush's Yasnapati and {F#her}{M#his} companion are here. There is a task you can help her successfully complete.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: It is no hard matter, though as you know, Sorush has been close with the Order of Skeptics and humans, while drifting further from Pari traditions.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: I would like to ask you to serve as an audience and listen to Sorush recount the past. A Bloomguard should naturally be able to speak of historical events, yes?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Of course.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If all we need to do is hear Sorush tell a story, it does sound pretty simple.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Then, I leave this to you two. As for the training that Sorush must complete by herself, I will let her know momentarily. You two merely need to accompany her.

choices.text: The Order of Skeptics even constantly makes mistakes in its official documents...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah. When we went to find Rashnu, the truth was entirely different from what they had down in their archives. They don't even know what's going on.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, stop being so strict!

talks.objective: Head to the specified location and complete the trial

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is this the last stop for our first day? We're pretty familiar with this place, seeing how we've been here plenty of times.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Hmph? If the Pale Floater is so confident, then why not swap roles with me? I will play the audience, you be the speaker.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah. Let's give it a try. Here comes Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The place before us — covered with flowers and flowing water — is the Vourukasha Oasis. This place doesn't have... uh... Right! This place isn't infested by the demons of Dev, and is the home of the Pari.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There are many Pari here. The best among them is one called Zurvan.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sorush, you were born here too, right? Though you were different from the other Pari...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: For example, while the other Pari only sound kinda weird when they speak, you sound *really* weird! Hmm. You all came from the same waters, but why is it that only you are so strange...

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Hey!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's not lying. When you were speaking to the Order of Skeptics, your words were kinda weird. Well, the Skeptics themselves sounded weird too. So there's that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew! Paimon thought all the other Pari were going to be exactly like you. In fact, Paimon was worried about that until we finally got to the Vourukasha Oasis and met Zurvan.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then, we found out that only you are like... Uh, how should Paimon put this... you have a particular way of speaking to the Order of Skeptics, right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It seems the Order of Skeptics had too much of an influence on her.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Uh... I will not deny that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seeing as you have no objections, Paimon will keep going. There is a big stump in the Vourukasha Oasis—

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Pale Floater, you absolute...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, it's the "Harvisptokhm" in the Vourukasha Oasis! Man, these Pari names sure are a mouthful. And, it totally is a big stump, isn't it...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon remembers you saying that the stump is also a god, and that the Pari have a deep relationship with it.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Though these are indeed the facts... Letting the Pale Floater describe them would be too unflattering. I shall resume the role of the speaker.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright... but Paimon thought she was making it easy to understand.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Hmph... Regardless, five hundred years ago, our great god gave all to quell the disaster afflicting this place. As such, all the Amrita here is the last gift from the divine.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Nourished by the Amrita, the Harvisptokhm and the Pari emerged. The eldest of the Pari, and my elder... is Zurvan.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: My birth came much later, so I was not a personal witness to those events. I heard my elder speak of it but...

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Elder Zurvan clearly associated with the Order of Skeptics when they were first established, but after my birth, all contact seemed to be lost between them.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Though my elder has long stated the importance of Pari traditions, she rarely mentions the past in detail when she speaks with me. Instead, it was the Order of Skeptics...

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Who enthusiastically shared the results of their historical research with me, and approved of my wish to follow in the footsteps of the divine bird.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? So after that, you slowly drifted away from the other Pari and learned your strange way of speaking from the Order of Skeptics?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Oh... I suppose that can be seen as correct. Objectively speaking.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It sounds like a rebellious phase...

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: A rebellious phase... I heard the humans in the Order of Skeptics mention something about this. They said the researchers in the forest experienced a "Satyavada Life" or something like that. Is this "rebellious phase" a similar thing that humans progress through?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, no! They're not the same thing at all!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Generally, kids going through a rebellious phase will resist the care of their parents and try to assert their independence. That's what Paimon's heard anyway.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, just like you did.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Hmph. My past has little to do with my present. Whatever can be said, I have now returned to the Vourukasha Oasis and earned the Khvarena's favor.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're amazing, Sorush!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Never mind, Pale Floater. It means nothing to be patronized by one as immature as you.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: That's all for today. Yasnapati, do you or the Pale Floater wish to ask anything?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Speaking of, are the Pari and Aranara related in any way?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: ...Why do you ask this?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Because the Pari and Aranara are both small...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But are still capable of great things.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You describe your adventures with Arama and all the other Aranara to Sorush...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Hmmm... How very important Festival Utsava appears to be. I heard my elder mention it once, but only thought of it as little more than a joyful gathering for the Aranara.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: But... if the Aranara have their own day, why do we Pari possess nothing of equivalence? I must mention this to my elder...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why do you want a Pari Festival? Is it because you can eat lots of tasty snacks during a festival?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Of course not! The Pari Festival should... should have humans offering their odes and songs to us, while I get to choose the best singer of the lot.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That doesn't sound like a festival at all. Well, not for the attending humans, anyway. It's more like a high-pressure competition.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: But it is an enjoyable celebration for me, yes? Hence, I believe my elder may also enjoy such an occasion.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Perhaps... Zurvan is right. For Sorush to become a so-called Bloomguard, she might need a bit more training...

choices.text: Maybe you can think of it as a necessary process for growth...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's not entirely like the Satyavada Life thing that the researchers experience. In fact, Paimon's heard that plenty of human children experience it...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Speaking of, since we were on the topic of the Pari's birth, have you encountered the familiars of the forest?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Familiars of the forest?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Indeed. The ones long called the Aranara.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: I only heard them mentioned by my elders. I heard they are not free to fly as we Pari are, but with their bond to the vegetation, they can stride the mud without restraints.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: I find it hard to picture such a scene... Are they like Wenut?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: But they do have their own festival. On that arrival of their day of celebration, the Aranara will gather together and enjoy a carefree time as one.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Sometimes I wonder, if the Aranara have their own day, why do we Pari possess nothing of equivalence? When I asked my elder, she seemed hollow of interest regarding the matter.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seems like Zurvan had this training regimen all planned out a long time ago. Guess Sorush was always going to have to do these things, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Hmm. This is a sign that the elder has always favored me.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Yasnapati. And Floater. Bear witness to my heroic feats.
